behavioral_effects: Pre-commit is installed from the repository root. Hygiene hooks are scoped away from frontend/, which keeps its own husky and lint-staged layer, so no frontend file is reformatted.
A governance job runs first in CI: clean rebuild of every generated document, diff-fail, the self-test suite, and a sync that must write nothing.
governance check accepts filenames positionally as well as via --files, because pre-commit passes staged files positionally.
governance snapshot-mcp-connections collects a sanitized aggregate inventory, over a DSN or through docker exec when the database publishes no host port.
The end-of-file hygiene hook added a missing trailing newline to docs/Critique_Response on its first pass over the existing tree.
compatibility_impact: The pre-commit configuration moved from backend/ to the repository root. Anyone with hooks already installed must re-run make install; the old path no longer exists, so a stale installation silently stops running rather than failing loudly. The four documentation and Makefile references were updated together. No application behaviour changed.
limitations: The change-record requirement is evaluated against the working tree, and against a commit range only when --since is passed. CI does not pass it, so on a clean checkout that rule has nothing to evaluate and the pre-commit hook is the real enforcement point.

The Trivy scan is unchanged and still cannot fail the build. Phase 5 pilots the maturity ladder on paper only: the rule carries explicit promotion criteria and the exception records the choice. Flipping exit-code now would promote a policy whose finding volume nobody has looked at, which is what the ladder exists to prevent.
Eighteen policy rules still report as not-yet-enforced. Four need the Phase 6 import graph, four are manual by nature, and the rest await extractors that Milestone 1 does not include.
The MCP snapshot covers one local development database with a single user. It is enough to inform the approval-gating decision, not to characterise production.
reason: Blueprint Phase 5 attaches the checks to the events that matter. Until now governance only ran when someone chose to run it, which means a stale manifest or an unrecorded governed change survives until the next person happens to look. The pre-commit layer catches it before the commit and CI catches it before the merge. The pre-commit config moves to the repository root because governance checks are repo-wide and the blueprint is explicit that this repository gets one hook framework rather than a third.
risks: The CI governance job installs both the governance tool and the backend, because the OpenAPI export needs the backend environment. That makes it the slowest gate to start and couples it to backend dependency resolution: a broken backend lockfile now fails the governance job as well as the test job.

Promoting the pre-commit config to the root means a developer with the old backend-scoped hooks installed gets no hooks at all until they re-run make install, and nothing warns them. Re-running make install is the fix, but the failure is silent.
rollback: git revert this commit, then re-run make install to reinstall hooks from the restored backend path. The governance CI job disappears with the workflow hunk; the other five jobs are untouched. The MCP evidence snapshot lives only in the gitignored cache and is unaffected either way — delete .cache/repo-governance/evidence/ if it should not persist. Reverting does not remove psycopg from the governance virtual environment; re-run uv sync --project tools/repo_governance without the evidence extra if that matters.
security_impact: Positive. A private-key scan now runs repo-wide on every commit, and the fast governance check — which includes the credential and connection-URL scanner over every governance artifact — runs whenever a governed file is staged. CI rebuilds every generated document in a clean checkout and fails on any difference, so a manifest that no longer follows from its sources cannot reach main unnoticed. The one-off MCP connection snapshot was taken under the runtime-evidence rules: aggregate counts only, URLs reduced to host at capture time, written to the gitignored cache, referenced from the manifest by ID and summary. It found 11 connections, all with explicit tool allowlists, and two bearer connections carrying no encrypted token — consistent with the credential living in the URL, which is the storage-design finding this evidence was collected to inform.
